preview.pickHint: Pick the type and the dates to see which days count.
preview.sandwichNote: {{name}} follows the sandwich rule: days off between two leave days count as leave.

apply.title: Apply for leave
apply.contactHintThem: A phone number, in case the ward needs to reach them.
apply.contactHintYou: A phone number, in case the ward needs to reach you.

chain.approveAsHrTitle: You'll approve as HR (override), in place of {{who}}

msg.rejected: Leave rejected. The employee is told.
msg.rejectedHr: Leave rejected (HR override). The employee is told.
msg.rejectedAtStep: Leave rejected at step {{step}} of {{total}}. The employee is told.
msg.rejectedAtStepHr: Leave rejected at step {{step}} of {{total}} (HR override). The employee is told.
msg.approvedHr: Leave approved by HR override. The days come off the balance.
msg.approvedHrMulti: Leave approved by HR override — the remaining steps were not needed. The days come off the balance.
msg.approvedAll: Leave approved — all {{total}} steps are done. The days come off the balance.
msg.stepRecorded: Your approval is recorded (step {{step}} of {{total}}). Now waiting for {{who}}.

chain.waitingForAnyone: Waiting for anyone who approves leave (HR)
chain.decideAsHr: You can decide this as HR (override), in place of {{who}}.
chain.yours: This step is yours to decide.
chain.approveMsgHr: It is waiting for {{who}}. As HR you finalise it now; it is recorded as an HR override. The days come off the balance.
chain.approveMsgHrMulti: It is waiting for {{who}}. As HR you finalise it now — the remaining steps are not needed; it is recorded as an HR override. The days come off the balance.
chain.approveMsgNext: Step {{step}} of {{total}}. It then goes to {{next}}.
chain.approveMsgFinal: The days come off the balance.
chain.rejectMsgHr: As HR (override) — it is waiting for {{who}}. The employee sees the reason.
chain.sayWhy: Say why it is not approved.

page.title: Leave
page.subtitle: Staff time off from request to approval, the balances behind it, and the leave setup.
page.requestedWaiting: Leave requested for {{name}} — waiting for approval.

drawer.cancelMsgApproved: The {{days}} already approved go back to {{name}}’s {{code}} balance.
drawer.sayWhy: Say why in a few words.
drawer.cancelledApproved: Leave cancelled — the days are back on the balance.
drawer.subtitle: Leave request
drawer.daysNote: Holidays and days off inside the range are not listed — they don’t count unless the sandwich rule applies.

requests.hintMine: A request reaches you when it is your step. Show › All requests lists everyone’s.
requests.hintAll: Staff apply from My workspace; HR can request on their behalf.

adjust.title: Adjust balance — {{name}}
adjust.placeholderOpening: Balance carried over from the old system
adjust.ledgerNote: The leave ledger is never edited — this adds an entry, and the balance is the sum of the entries.

compOff.title: Credit comp-off — {{name}}
compOff.workedOnHint: The day off or holiday they worked.
compOff.onceNote: A worked day can be credited only once.

balance.subtitle: Leave balances
balance.noType: No leave type applies to this employee.

balances.note: Available = balance less what is waiting for approval. A dot means the leave type does not apply to that person (gender or staff category).

policies.label: Leave policies
policies.hint: How each leave type is credited, carried over and taken.

approvals.label: Approval chains
approvals.hint: Who approves a leave request, step by step — by leave type, department, staff category or length.

calendars.label: Holiday calendars
calendars.hint: The holiday list per branch — days off for staff on the weekly-off pattern, never charged as leave.

regularizations.label: Regularizations
regularizations.hint: Attendance corrections are approved in Attendance › Corrections, next to the punches they fix.

overtime.label: Overtime
overtime.hint: Time worked beyond the shift, or a day off worked, given back as comp-off or pay.

corrections.title: Attendance corrections
corrections.text: A correction adds the missing punches and the day is worked out again — so it is approved where the punches are: Attendance › Corrections.

holidays.title: Holidays
holidays.subtitle: The hospital’s holiday list, per branch. Staff on the weekly-off pattern get these days off; rostered staff follow their roster.

holidayCalendar.restrictedText: Restricted (optional) holiday — not a day off for everyone
holidayCalendar.restrictedHint: Staff take it from their leave if they want it.
holidayCalendar.deleteMsg: {{date}} becomes an ordinary working day again.
holidayCalendar.emptyHint: Add the national and festival holidays the hospital observes.

example.monthlyThis: Someone who joined years ago has earned {{earned}} of {{quota}} days so far this leave year ({{perMonth}} a month, on the 1st). Someone joining today starts this month.
example.monthlyNext: Someone who joined years ago has earned {{earned}} of {{quota}} days so far this leave year ({{perMonth}} a month, on the 1st). Someone joining today starts next month.
example.upfront: Everyone already here had the whole {{quota}} days at the start of the leave year. Someone joining today gets {{rest}} for the rest of it.
example.onConfirmation: Nothing during probation. On their confirmation date (set on the employee) someone gets the rest of that leave year pro-rata — {{rest}} if confirmed today — then the full {{quota}} at each new leave year.

credited.title: How it’s credited
credited.hint: When the days land in the employee’s balance (the ledger).
credited.confirmationNote: Uses each employee’s confirmation date (end of probation) — set it on the employee record. Without one, nothing is credited.

rules.title: Request rules
rules.negative: No limit — may go below zero
rules.negativeHint: For leave granted on need (maternity, LOP).

counting.title: How days are counted
counting.hint: Weekly offs, rostered offs and holidays inside a request are never charged…
counting.sandwichHint: …unless this is on: then days off between two leave days count as leave.

yearEnd.title: Year end & pay
yearEnd.carryHint: Blank = no cap · 0 = lapses at year end
yearEnd.paidHint: Unpaid leave counts as loss of pay.
yearEnd.compOffHint: Credited for overtime and days off worked (Setup › Overtime).

policies.inUseHint: A retired type keeps its history but can’t be applied for.
policies.intro: One policy per leave type. Balances are a ledger: every credit, lapse, leave taken and adjustment is an entry, and accruals run on their own each month.
policies.emptyHint: Add a policy per leave type.

typeHint.REPORTING_MANAGER: The employee’s reporting manager (set on the employee). HR stands in when there is none or they have no login.
typeHint.DEPARTMENT_HEAD: The head of the employee’s department (Administration › Departments). HR stands in when none is set.
typeHint.HR: Anyone whose role can approve leave (hrms.leave.approve), within their data scope.
typeHint.SPECIFIC_USERS: Any one of the people picked here.
typeHint.ROLE: Anyone holding one of the roles picked here.

chains.name: Name
chains.inUseHint: An unused chain is kept but never picked.
chains.minDaysHint: Requests of at least this many days. Blank = any length.
chains.stepNameHint: Shown to the employee: “With …”. Blank = the approver type.
chains.skipRepeatsHint: Skip a step whose only approver is the applicant, or whose approvers already said yes at an earlier step. Off: HR stands in for the applicant.
chains.moveOnHint: A step with no decision this long passes to the next one — or to HR at the last. Blank = never.
chains.selfNote: Nobody approves their own leave. HR (Leave › edit) can still approve or reject at any step; it is recorded as an HR override.
chains.deleteMsg: Requests already under way keep the chain they started with. New requests fall to the next matching chain, or the default.
chains.intro: Each leave request follows the highest-priority chain in use that matches it. The request waits on one step at a time — the days stay held from the balance — and is charged only at the last approval. A rejection at any step ends it.
chains.defaultNote: Default (no chain matches): the employee’s reporting manager decides. HR — anyone who approves leave — stands in when there is no manager, the manager has no login, or the manager is the applicant.
chains.emptyHint: Every request uses the default: reporting manager, else HR. Add a chain for, say, doctors’ long leave: manager → head of department → HR.

overtime.creditHint: Suggested {{days}} for this much time. It lands on the leave ledger today.
overtime.payrollNote: Payroll pays it with the month’s salary at the overtime rate (Payroll settings).
overtime.notePlaceholder: Covered the ICU night after a sick call
overtime.rejectMsg: It is not paid as overtime and no comp-off is credited. The employee is told why.
overtime.sayWhy: Say why in a few words.
overtime.intro: From attendance: net time worked beyond the shift (breaks taken out), or a day off worked — of at least {{min}} minutes (Attendance › Setup › Rules). Approve as comp-off to credit the leave ledger, or as paid overtime for payroll.
overtime.emptyHint: Overtime shows here once a day with extra time is over.
